# Arduino 8-Step Synth — initial documentation

Documentation version: 0.1 · Reviewed: 27 November 2026

This document describes the two source files currently in this folder. Findings come from source inspection; compilation, browser operation, wiring, and physical hardware have not yet been tested.

## Project overview

An eight-step monophonic synthesizer runs in the browser, controlled by an Arduino over USB serial. The Arduino reads four potentiometers and a rotary encoder with a push button, and displays the sequence and parameters on a 20×4 I²C LCD.

**Audio is generated by the computer, not the Arduino.** The sketch contains no oscillator, audio output, MIDI output, or standalone sequencer clock. The browser owns the sequence, playback timing, and sound engine; the Arduino mirrors browser state on its LCD.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Self-contained interface, Web Serial connection, eight-step editor, and Web Audio synthesizer. CSS and JavaScript are embedded; there are no external package imports. |
| `sketch_nov27a.ino` | Arduino firmware for analog inputs, encoder decoding, serial messages, and the physical LCD. Uses `Wire.h` and `LiquidCrystal_I2C.h`. |
| `README.md` | This initial source-based project documentation. |

The HTML identifies the board as an Arduino Uno. The actual board model, component models, library versions, and wiring have not been independently confirmed. No schematic, dependency lockfile, build configuration, or tests are included.

## Hardware connections expected by the code

| Component / signal | Arduino connection | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Potentiometer 1 wiper | A1 | Pitch transpose |
| Potentiometer 2 wiper | A2 | Low-pass filter cutoff |
| Potentiometer 3 wiper | A3 | Tempo |
| Potentiometer 4 wiper | A0 | Tremolo rate and depth |
| Encoder CLK | Digital 2 | Quadrature input, interrupt on CHANGE |
| Encoder DT | Digital 3 | Quadrature input, interrupt on CHANGE |
| Encoder SW | Digital 4 | Active-low push button |
| LCD | Board I²C bus, address `0x27` | 20 columns × 4 rows |

Encoder inputs use `INPUT_PULLUP`. Firmware assumes four quadrature transitions per detent and a 10-bit analog range of 0–1023. Potentiometer resistance, supply wiring, LCD supply voltage, and the board-specific SDA/SCL pins are not specified in these files; verify these against the actual hardware before wiring.

## Controls and parameter mapping

| Control | Reported value | Browser effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 / PIT | −100 to +100 | Integer transpose: `round(PIT × 12 / 100)`, spanning −12 to +12 semitones |
| A2 / CUT | 0–100 | Exponential cutoff from 90 Hz to 16,000 Hz; low-pass filter Q = 1 |
| A3 / BPM | Raw 0–100 | `40 + 2 × raw`, spanning 40–240 BPM |
| A0 / LFO | 0–100 | Tremolo frequency 0.4–11.4 Hz and modulation depth 0–0.65; zero depth at 0 |

The firmware samples and reports knobs approximately every 50 ms. For each input it discards one reading, averages 16 readings, then applies smoothing with coefficient 0.15. Percentage values change when the smoothed value differs by more than 0.7; pitch is calculated separately from its smoothed analog value.

Browser-only controls provide Start/Stop, waveform (sawtooth, square, triangle, sine), sound level, and a shared octave selection from 2 to 5. Defaults are sawtooth, level 35%, and octave 3. Before hardware data arrives, parameters are PIT 0, CUT 50, BPM 120, and LFO 0.

## Sequence editing and playback

- Eight steps start with `C E G B A G E D`.
- Each step offers REST or one of the 12 chromatic pitch classes. All steps share the selected octave.
- One step is an eighth note: duration in seconds is `60 / BPM / 2`.
- Start begins from step 1. Stop closes the audio context; the next Start creates a new one.
- While stopped or playing, turning the physical encoder selects a step. Pressing it toggles note-edit mode; turning it then changes the note. Selection and notes wrap at either end.
- Browser −/+ buttons follow the same mode: they select steps outside edit mode and change notes inside edit mode.
- Focusing a note dropdown selects its step and exits edit mode. Changing a dropdown updates the sequence.
- Green indicates playback, gold outlines selection, and orange indicates editing.

The browser and physical encoder both allow editing during playback. Upload the updated sketch to enable this on the hardware. Notes already scheduled by the browser may play their previous value before the edit is heard.

## Sound engine

Signal path:

`Oscillator → low-pass filter → note envelope → master gain → tremolo gain → computer audio output`

A second oscillator modulates tremolo gain. The pitch formula is `440 × 2^((MIDI − 69) / 12)`, with MIDI pitch derived from the shared octave, step note, and transpose control. REST leaves the note envelope at zero.

Each sounding step has an 8 ms attack and a release ramp over roughly the final 35 ms of its gate. Gate length is the smaller of 72% of the step duration and 300 ms. The sound-level slider scales master gain to a maximum of 0.28; tremolo gain has a base value of 1.

The scheduler runs every 25 ms and schedules approximately 120 ms ahead using Web Audio time. Separate browser timers update the visible playhead and send it to the Arduino. These display updates are not sample-accurate, and edits may not affect notes already scheduled.

## Serial protocol

Connection speed is **115200 baud**. Messages are text lines terminated by a newline. Arduino `Serial.println` sends CRLF; both receiving paths accommodate it. Step indices on the wire are **0–7**, while the browser labels them 1–8.

| Direction | Format | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arduino → browser | `pitch,cutoff,thirdKnob,lfo` | Four knob readings, e.g. `0,50,40,0` maps to 120 BPM |
| Arduino → browser | `E,<delta>` | Signed encoder detent count; emitted while stopped or playing |
| Arduino → browser | `B` | Debounced button press; emitted while stopped or playing |
| Browser → Arduino | `N,<16 characters>` | Eight fixed-width two-character note cells |
| Browser → Arduino | `S,<playing>,<selected>,<editing>` | Playback/edit flags as 0/1 and selected index |
| Browser → Arduino | `P,<index>` | Current playback step |

Natural notes are padded with a space, sharps occupy both characters, and REST is `--`. For example, the default sequence message is `N,C E G B A G E D `, including the final space before the newline. The firmware requires exactly 18 characters for an `N` message, excluding the line ending.

The browser serializes writes through a promise queue. Its `sync()` sends notes and state, plus playhead during playback. Connection triggers immediate synchronization and another attempt after 1.8 seconds. There is no handshake, acknowledgement, protocol version, or automatic reconnect.

## LCD behavior

Physical LCD rows:

1. Eight two-character sequence cells.
2. A `^` marker under the current playback step while playing; blank while stopped.
3. PIT and CUT values.
4. BPM and LFO values.

The cursor always follows the selected step and blinks during note editing, including during playback. The separate marker on row 2 follows playback. The browser's virtual LCD is similar but replaces the sequence row with `EDIT STEP …` while editing; it is not an exact physical-display emulator.

## Initial run procedure

These steps are inferred from the source and have not yet been verified on hardware.

1. Confirm the board, wiring, LCD address, and component voltage requirements.
2. Open the sketch in the Arduino IDE. If it requests a matching sketch folder, place `sketch_nov27a.ino` in a folder named `sketch_nov27a`.
3. Install a compatible `LiquidCrystal_I2C` library supporting `init()`, select the board and serial port, and upload. The repository does not pin a library implementation or version.
4. Close any Serial Monitor or other application holding the port.
5. Open `index.html` in a browser exposing `navigator.serial`. The page recommends desktop Chrome or Edge and opening the file directly; actual browser support and permissions still need verification.
6. Click **Connect Arduino** and choose its port. Check that knob values update and the physical LCD receives the sequence.
7. Start with low computer volume, then click **Start Sequencer**. Sound comes from the computer's selected audio output.

The page can also run without an Arduino: click Start to use its initial parameter values and edit notes with the browser controls. There are no browser sliders for PIT, CUT, BPM, or LFO. Disconnecting preserves the last received values and does not stop audio, even though the status message refers to “demo values.”

## Known gaps and next verification

- No persistence: refreshing the page resets notes and browser settings.
- No confirmed hardware/build test or browser compatibility test is recorded.
- Serial write failures are silently caught. Connection status does not guarantee that the LCD received an update.
- The firmware uses a 64-byte input buffer and basic parsing; oversized lines are truncated rather than explicitly rejected as a whole.
- Browser state is authoritative, but there is no acknowledgement that the Arduino applied it. Disconnecting during playback can leave the Arduino showing a stale playback marker until state is resynchronized or the board resets.
- The physical display shows pitch as −100…+100 and cutoff/LFO as percentages, rather than semitones or Hz.

Suggested first checks: compile/upload with recorded board and library versions; verify all four knob mappings and LCD rows; test stopped selection/editing and wraparound; test REST, octave, waveform, and Start/Stop; verify encoder selection, note editing, and the separate LCD playback marker during playback; then test disconnect/reconnect both while stopped and while playing.
